title: Distracted by Talent
coreMove: Look past easy performance and ask who keeps improving when the work stops flattering them.
sourcePressure: Correct the habit of overreading quick aptitude and underreading repeated effort.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Thinking the point is that talent does not matter at all.

sourceAnchors.name: David Luong
sourceAnchors.detail: At Lowell High School, he began in a lower-level algebra class, kept turning in perfect work, moved up, and later became a rocket scientist.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: David Luong is the kind of student a talent-first room can misread because his work arrives quietly before his label changes.

sourceAnchors.name: Lower East Side classroom
sourceAnchors.detail: Duckworth left consulting at age 27 to teach seventh-grade math and saw quick learners earn poor grades while steadier students rose.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The classroom made the talent bias visible in rows of notebooks, not in a theory.
